# keyrx

> Solana and EVM vanity address grinder. One seed, unlimited addresses, keys for every wallet. Offline. Open. Verified. The mark is a record. What it seals comes next.
>
> One seed phrase is a tree of addresses; keyrx
> derives the expensive prefix once and walks the account index - 20-60x the
> throughput of `solana-keygen grind --use-mnemonic`. Every match writes the
> address, its derivation path, the seed phrase, and the keypair in both
> wallet-import forms (base58 for Phantom, JSON byte array for Solflare and
> solana-keygen). One Rust binary. No daemon, no service, no network.
>
> `--chain evm` (0.4.0): Ethereum and every EVM chain - the same mnemonic walk on
> secp256k1 at m/44'/60'/0'/0/N, keccak addresses in EIP-55 case; hex patterns,
> any case by default, `--checksum` for EIP-55 case as typed; the match writes the
> 0x hex private key MetaMask and Rabby import. Matches under matches/evm/.

The site is a terminal UI rendered in JavaScript with a real toy grind in a
Web Worker; nothing leaves the browser. This file carries the same content
as plain text.

## Install

    cargo install keyrx && clear && keyrx    # or: git clone https://github.com/keyrx/keyrx && cargo install --path .
    keyrx verify                 # run first, always: base58, derivation, the pinned solana-keygen answer, the BIP39 passphrase vector
    keyrx bench --indices 128    # this machine's real rate; estimate uses it
    keyrx estimate --ends-with KEYRX --count 10    # odds; time to one match and to all ten
    keyrx grind --ends-with KEYRX --indices 128
    keyrx grind --ends-with KEYRX --count 10       # ten matches, one file
    keyrx grind --ends-with KEYRX --indices 8      # Phantom by seed: the match is at most 8 "add account" clicks away
    keyrx grind --ends-with KEYRX --passphrase     # BIP39 passphrase: prompted, hidden, never stored; import that address by key
    keyrx grind --starts-with Key --ends-with RX   # both ends; --ignore-case for any case (32x likelier for five letters)
    keyrx show                   # every match file; keyrx show KEYRX --keys reads one (seeds/keys withheld by default)
    keyrx --update               # cargo install keyrx && clear && keyrx, as one flag

## What a match writes

Five lines, in a mode-0600 file inside a mode-0700 directory of its own
(~/.local/share/keyrx/matches/, named after the pattern; every printed path
is a terminal hyperlink that opens the folder): address, path, seed, privkey
(base58 keypair), keypair (JSON byte array) - and, for a --passphrase grind,
one line saying so: the seed alone will not reach that address, the keys will. A key import lands
on the exact address in one paste as a standalone account - the file IS the
backup. Importing the seed instead places the address inside a recoverable
HD wallet at the printed path; Phantom reaches account N by N "add account"
clicks (grind with --indices 8 for that), Solflare takes the path directly.

## Verified

SLIP-0010 identical to solana-keygen at both path styles (pinned as tests);
ground hits re-derive from their own seed; both key encodings round-trip
through `solana-keygen pubkey` to the same address; 50,000 pubkeys x 10
suffix lengths agree with the full base58 encoding. Bench 24.4x baseline at
128 indices, 32.2x at 256.

MIT. Import and verify the address before funding. Match files hold seed
phrases and keys - treat them like a key.
